title: 4-bit Vector NOT
description: Create a Verilog module that inverts all bits of a 4-bit vector. This is your introduction to working with multi-bit signals (buses)! Instead of a single wire, you'll work with a 4-bit wide signal. Each bit should be independently inverted - if input bit is 0, corresponding output bit is 1, and vice versa. This operation is fundamental in digital systems for bitwise negation, complement operations, and data manipulation. Understanding vector operations is crucial because real circuits process multiple bits simultaneously - processors work with 32-bit or 64-bit data!
hint: Use the bitwise NOT operator (~). For example: assign out = ~in;

test_cases.description: Invert all zeros to all ones
Invert all ones to all zeros

constraints: Input port must be named in (4-bit vector)
Output port must be named out (4-bit vector)

title: AND Gate
description: Implement a 2-input AND gate. The output should be logic high only when both inputs are high. Use combinational logic with continuous assignment.
hint: Use the & operator or write: assign out = a & b;

title: OR Gate
description: Implement a 2-input OR gate. The output should be logic high when at least one input is high. Use continuous assignment statement.
hint: Use the | operator: assign out = a | b;

examples.explanation: At least one input high, output high

title: NAND Gate
description: Implement a 2-input NAND gate. This is an AND gate followed by an inverter. Output is low only when both inputs are high.

title: D Flip-Flop
description: Implement a positive-edge triggered D flip-flop. The output q should capture the input d value only at rising clock edges and hold it otherwise.

examples.explanation: Output captures input on rising edge

title: Half Adder
description: Implement a half adder that adds two single-bit inputs a and b, producing sum and carry outputs. Sum = a XOR b, Carry = a AND b.
hint: assign sum = a ^ b; assign carry = a & b;
